detail.longDescription:
Another Qwen 3.8 test!

Just now, completely out of the blue, I asked Qwen to write me a Bash script that would upscale all images in a directory 2x with Real-ESRGAN.

All instructions were given in German.

Qwen read the Real-ESRGAN README to figure out how the program works and picked the correct 2x upscaling model. It then searched the directory for PNG files and noticed that I hadn't put any PNGs in there yet xD

It wrote the script anyway.

I then asked whether it had actually checked if the Real-ESRGAN binary was executable. In the meantime, I had added the PNGs to the directory.

Qwen checked it, made the binary executable with chmod +x and then ran the script. All images were successfully upscaled!

Next, I wanted the output automatically converted to JPEG because the PNG files were huge. I also wanted all PNGs removed from the output directory.

Qwen read the README again and rewrote the script so Real-ESRGAN would directly output JPEG files instead D:

And the whole thing ran LOCALLY using Qwen 3.8 through Ollama + OpenCode. No cloud, no API, no remote agent.

The only downside? My GPU (RX 6700 XT) has "only" 12 GB of VRAM -.-

With another 12 GB, this probably wouldn't have taken 25 minutes.

The next generation really needs min. 24 GB of VRAM in the mid-range!
